Answers we can give you now

Rather than leave you with nothing while those are written, here are the short versions with the evidence attached.

Why hair dryers fail

Across 8,261 Canadian reviews, the median reported failure time was 5.5 months and the mean 6.0 months. Only 0.8% failed out of the box, so this is a wear-out problem, not a bad batch.

Failure modeMentions
Stopped working entirely601
Cord / connector failure417
Switch or button failure300
Motor / airflow degradation196
Smoking or catching fire182

The practical takeaway: check the cord strain relief where it enters the handle on arrival. It is the second most common failure point and it is visible.

Why your dryer smells like burning

215 reviews mention burning or plastic smell, and 84% of them are negative. In several cases a burning smell preceded a heating element failure within months. If your dryer smells like burning, stop using it and contact the seller or brand.

What wattage does and does not tell you

Wattage describes power draw, not drying speed. A modern high-speed brushless dryer can move more air than a 1875W conventional dryer while drawing less. This is why our guides rank on airflow evidence rather than wattage, and why “2000W” in a product title tells you less than it appears to.

Voltage, in one table

SituationWhat you need
Using a Canadian dryer at home120V, ALCI plug — standard
Taking it to Europe, UK or AustraliaDual voltage 110–220V and a plug adapter
Taking it to the United StatesNothing — same 120V, same plug
Using a US-purchased dryer in CanadaIt works, but warranty service may mean shipping to the US

Voltage was the single most-discussed topic in our dataset at 785 mentions — ahead of noise, weight and price. It is the most common travel mistake in this category.

How we write a guide

Each guide has to earn its place, so we apply the same standard as to our reviews.

  1. The direct answer comes first, before the explanation — because that is the part you came for
  2. Every claim is labelled as review analysis, listing data, buyer feedback, a manufacturer claim, or our own measurement
  3. We name what we have not verified. Where a guide depends on bench measurements we have not taken yet, it says so
  4. No number without a source. If a figure cannot be traced, it does not appear

Our method is published in full on how we test, and our rules are in our editorial policy. If a guide concludes that a particular specification matters, you will usually find the models that do it well in our best hair dryers guide or compared head to head in comparisons.

Frequently asked questions

What is the difference between ionic and ceramic hair dryers? They are not alternatives. Ceramic describes the heating element, which heats more evenly than a bare metal coil. Ionic describes a generator that emits negative ions to reduce static. Many dryers use both, which is why treating them as competing categories is a mistake.

Does higher wattage mean a better hair dryer? Not on its own. Wattage describes power draw, not drying speed. A modern high-speed brushless dryer can move more air than a 1875W conventional dryer while drawing less power, which is why our guides rank on airflow evidence rather than on wattage claims.

Why does my hair dryer smell like burning? A persistent burning smell is the most common precursor reviewers describe before a dryer dies. It appeared in 215 reviews in our dataset with 84% of them negative, and in several cases a burnt smell preceded a heating element failure. Stop using it and contact the seller or brand.

Can I use my Canadian hair dryer in Europe? Only if it is dual voltage. Most Canadian dryers are 120V only, and plugging one into a 220–240V outlet will damage it, sometimes immediately. Use a plug adapter only where the dryer supports the local voltage; otherwise you need a dual-voltage model.

Why do hair dryers break so often? Across 8,261 Canadian reviews the median reported failure was 5.5 months, and only 0.8% failed out of the box — so this is a wear-out problem rather than a defective-batch problem. The most common failure modes were complete stoppage at 601 mentions and cord or connector failure at 417.
